title: Gentbox message v1
description: What a sender POSTs to /v1/messages. Field names are camelCase. Unknown top-level fields are rejected so a typo never passes silently; `metadata` is the open extension point. Each message carries three independent fields, `type`, `urgent` and `blocking` (docs/adr/0007-message-type-urgency-blocking.md); any of them may be left to the rules. Optional `topic` and `thread` group the message: topic → thread → messages (docs/adr/0008-topics.md, docs/adr/0009-threads.md). See docs/architecture.md.

version.description: Schema major version. The hub rejects any other value with 422.

idempotencyKey.description: Sender-chosen key that makes retries safe: a second POST with the same key from the same source.agent returns the stored message instead of creating another. Not the message id: the hub assigns that (a ULID) and returns it.

topic.description: The Gentbox topic (not an ntfy topic): a project, a bigger undertaking, or a category for simple conversations. `{ "id": … }` names an existing topic; `{ "key": … }` names one by its stable key and creates it on first use, titled `title` or the key. The inline form never changes an existing topic; a message to a closed topic reopens it. Without `topic`: a rule-assigned topic, else the topic of the conversation's latest default thread, else the agent's implicit General topic (docs/adr/0009-threads.md).

thread.description: The thread within the topic: a version, a phase, or simply a conversation. `{ "id": … }` names an existing thread (and so its topic; a different `topic` is a 422). `{ "key": … }` names one within the resolved topic and creates it on first use. Without `thread`: a rule-assigned thread, else the conversation's default thread in that topic (an implicit `kind: "conversation"` thread, or an explicit one that took it over).

type.description: What the message asks of you. `decision_required`: the agent needs your answer (approve or deny, pick a choice, reply). `action_required`: you must do something yourself outside the conversation (sign in, add a key, review a pull request), then tell the agent it is done. `task_completed`: work finished. `generic`: everything else, kept for reference. Declared fields win over the rules (except a user rule with `override = true`); missing ones are filled by user rules, then built-in rules, then the default `generic`.

urgent.description: True when the message should reach you now: Time Sensitive on the Mac (and later the phone), breaks through quiet hours and Focus, shown with the red urgent badge and sorted above other messages. Never a title prefix (native notifications lead the subtitle with "Urgent ·"). Default false. Never true for `generic`.

blocking.description: What the agent does meanwhile. `non_blocking`: it keeps working and has planned for the answer to come later. `deferrable`: it has paused, but you may answer Defer to let it continue with work that needs no input. `blocking`: work cannot continue until you decide. Default `non_blocking`; always `non_blocking` for `task_completed` and `generic`.

event.description: The sender's own event name, dotted, for rules to match (e.g. `claude-code.notification.idle_prompt`). Never shown to the user.

title.description: A descriptive summary in plain words of what the agent asks or did, one line in every channel (e.g. "Allow Bash to run the ingest tests?", "Ingest auth accepts rotated tokens; 12 tests pass"). Never a command, path, URL or raw tool input: those go in `body`. The hub's title guard moves such text into the body and replaces the title, with a warning in the response (docs/adr/0010-descriptive-titles.md).

summary.description: Plain text: what is needed, or what was done, in plain words. The description of every notification, on the Mac and on the phone (unless the phone payload mode is minimal or the message is sensitive), and the inbox row. Same rule as `title`: no commands, paths, URLs or raw input; the hub's title guard moves them into `body`.

body.description: Markdown shown in the conversation detail and the rich popup. In the `summary` payload mode an excerpt trimmed to the 4 KB push budget goes to the own iOS app over APNs (ADR 0006); never to the ntfy fallback. The place for commands, paths, URLs and raw tool input, rendered as code boxes.

steps.description: The action plan of an `action_required` message: ordered, plain instructions that tell you how to complete the action, ticked off in the app's steps view. Required for `action_required` (the hub adds a fallback step and warns when missing; strict mode rejects). Only for `action_required`: with no declared type, `steps` makes it the default type. Commands, paths and raw input go in a step's `detail`, never its `text` (docs/adr/0011-action-plans.md).

actions.description: Buttons, in display order. The phone gets at most three, and answer buttons only when its payload mode shows what is asked (docs/architecture.md §9.3).

scope.description: For `task_completed`: `task` (default) for one finished task, `goal` when the agent reached its overall objective. Picks the notification title (Task complete / Goal complete).

awaitsResponse.description: True when the sender intends to long-poll /v1/messages/{id}/response. What counts is the live waiter (a poll in flight or ended under 10 s ago): answer buttons (approve, deny, choice, reply, done, defer) are offered only while one exists.

correlationKey.description: The slot this message occupies in its conversation. A new message with the key of an open message takes its slot in place (same notification, updated content) instead of pinging again, unless the open one has a live waiter and the new one has not; then it only counts as a repeat (docs/architecture.md §7).

rescinds.description: Withdraws other open messages of the same conversation by correlation key, as part of sending this one. The same as POST /v1/conversations/{agent}/{id}/rescind.

sensitive.description: True when even the title must not leave the Mac. The phone then gets only the title phrase for the type, whatever the payload mode.

createdAt.description: When the sender produced the event. The hub records its own receivedAt and orders by that.

expiresAt.description: After this instant the message moves to `expired`, its popup closes and a waiting sender gets status `expired`. Defaults by type and blocking level (docs/architecture.md §5.2).

metadata.description: Flat sender facts for rules and display (tool name, model, exit code). No secrets: metadata is stored and may be shown.

rescindReason.description: `resolved_elsewhere`: answered or handled in the session or another channel. `obsolete`: no longer needed. `superseded`: replaced by a newer message.

rescindRequest.description: Body of DELETE /v1/messages/{id} (reason only) and of POST /v1/conversations/{agent}/{id}/rescind (reason and correlation keys); also the `rescinds` field of a message.

topicKey.description: Stable key the agent chooses, unique per hub across all agents (e.g. `release-1.4`, `repo:gentbox`). Re-creating a topic with the same key returns the existing one.

symbol.description: SF Symbol name hint, e.g. `shippingbox`. The app shows it only if it is on its allowed list, else the default topic symbol.

color.description: Colour hint from the app's palette.

topicCreate.description: Body of POST /v1/topics: an upsert by `key`. Creating an existing key returns it unchanged (200 instead of 201); use PATCH to change it.

conversation.description: The conversation creating it, recorded in `createdBy`.

topicUpdate.description: Body of PATCH /v1/topics/{id}. Only the given fields change; `summary: null` clears it. Implicit (General) topics answer 409 to agents.

closeRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/topics/{id}/close and POST /v1/threads/{id}/close. Closing never touches open messages unless `rescindOpenMessages` is true; then every open message in the topic or thread is rescinded with `reason` (default `obsolete`). Closing a topic also closes its open threads.

topicRecord.description: A topic as the hub returns it (POST, PATCH, GET). Implicit topics (the per-agent General topic) have no `key`.

implicit.description: True for an agent's hub-managed General topic.

openMessages.description: Count of open and acknowledged messages.

agent.description: Stable agent id, lowercase (e.g. `claude-code`, `codex`). Rules and per-source settings key on it.

host.description: Machine name, when the sender runs on another machine than the hub.

conversation.description: The agent session the message belongs to. Coalescing, supersede and resolve all work within one conversation.

id.description: The agent's session id (Claude Code `session_id`). Unique per source.agent.

title.description: Descriptive conversation title; one that looks like a command or raw input is ignored by the hub (ADR 0010).

cwd.description: Working directory. Shown as the project name; never sent to the phone.

focusTarget.description: How the `open` action brings the conversation forward. The hub tries `url`, then `terminal`, then activates `bundleId`.

url.description: Deep link that opens the conversation (custom scheme or https). Only schemes on the user's allowlist are opened.

bundleId.description: macOS bundle id of the app hosting the session (e.g. `com.mitchellh.ghostty`, `com.anthropic.claudefordesktop`).

id.description: Unique within the message; returned to the sender as `actionId`.

value.description: For `choice`: the value returned to the sender. For `snooze`: minutes as a decimal string (default 15).

destructive.description: Shown in the destructive style and never offered as an ntfy one-tap button.

actionKind.description: Answers, returned to the waiting sender: approve and deny (fixed meaning), choice (returns its value), reply (returns free text), done (you did the thing an `action_required` message asked for), defer (only on `deferrable` messages: keep working on what needs no input; the message stays open as `non_blocking` and the hub adds this button by itself). The first answer other than defer closes the message. Non-answers, never returned: open (acknowledges and brings the conversation forward) and snooze (a local to Gentbox reminder after `value` minutes; tells the agent nothing).

actionResponse.description: Body of GET /v1/messages/{id}/response. Not part of the POST body; defined here so senders validate both ends against one file.

messageId.description: The hub-assigned message id (ULID) from the 201 response.

status.description: `pending`: open, poll again. `answered`: see actionKind and value. `deferred`: you chose Defer; keep working on what needs no input and poll again later, the message stays open as `non_blocking`. `dismissed`: you marked it done without answering. `rescinded`: withdrawn (see rescindReason). `expired`. On `dismissed`, `rescinded` and `expired` the sender falls back to its own prompt.

actionKind.description: Only answer kinds are ever returned (defer as status `deferred`).

value.description: The choice value or the reply text.

topicKind.description: Free-form hint the UI may show, never changing behaviour. Suggested: `project`, `category`, `other`; the hub's implicit General topics use `general`.

threadKey.description: Stable key the agent chooses, unique within its topic (e.g. `phase-3-ingest`, `v1.4`).

threadKind.description: Free-form hint the UI may show, never changing behaviour. Suggested: `version`, `phase`, `conversation`, `other`. With `kind: "conversation"` and `conversation.id` at creation, a thread takes over that conversation's implicit thread in its topic.

threadCreate.description: Body of POST /v1/threads: an upsert by `key` within the topic. Creating an existing key returns it unchanged (200 instead of 201). Without `topic` the topic is resolved as for a message. With `kind: "conversation"` and `conversation.id` it takes over that conversation's implicit thread in the topic, unless the conversation's default thread there is already explicit.

conversation.description: The conversation creating it, recorded in `createdBy`; with `kind: "conversation"` also the conversation whose implicit thread it takes over.

threadUpdate.description: Body of PATCH /v1/threads/{id}. Only the given fields change; `summary: null` clears it. Implicit threads answer 409 to agents.

threadMove.description: Body of PUT /v1/threads/{id}/topic: move the thread and its messages to another topic (409 if its key exists there).

messageThreadMove.description: Body of PUT /v1/messages/{id}/thread: move the message to another thread, or back to its default resolution with `thread: null`.

threadRecord.description: A thread as the hub returns it (POST, PATCH, GET). Implicit threads have no `key`.

implicit.description: True for a conversation's hub-managed default thread.

defaultFor.description: The conversation whose default thread in this topic this is, if any.

conversations.description: How many conversations have posted into it.

ingestResponse.description: Body of the 201 (or idempotent 200) response to POST /v1/messages.

warnings.description: Changes the hub made, for the sender to learn from (e.g. the title guard).

text.description: One plain instruction. Passes the title guard: no commands, paths, URLs or raw input.

detail.description: Markdown: commands in code blocks, paths, explanations.

url.description: `https`, or a scheme on the open allowlist (`claude-cli`, `claude`, `vscode`, `cursor`, `x-apple.systempreferences`). Opened only on tap, with the URL shown.
